artifacts.summary: Verdict-first report: every morphism-invariant language (L, L+, L*, L-open, L+ with same-state) is blind to recurrence by one compiled meta-theorem; state nominals/registers see recurrence and transposition but not determinism (compiled); since/until blind along any history-lifting map; blc is the only live limit-closure schema and the product keeps its countermodel; manuscript remark drafted for sub:Conclusion.

next_steps: Optional small port of probes 01-02 into the library (see Recommendation 1); manuscript remark per section 5.3; no plan/implementation implied by this research task.

memory_candidates.content: Blindness to recurrence in the task semantics reduces to one hypothesis: invariance of the truth predicate along the translation projection for lifted models (Probe653.classValid_iff_recurrenceFree_of_prodInvariant). Decision table for a new operator: consults one history's times only -> invariant along any HistMap (since/until); quantifies histories at the present time -> needs onto (box) or lift (stability, same-state); agreement on a ray -> needs the product's unique lift (open future/past); state identity across two times of one history -> not invariant (state registers, binder, standard propositional quantifiers).

State nominals/registers and time registers see disjoint frame features: state nominals define recurrence-freeness (recF_defines) but F-drift and F-translation validate the same hybrid sentences (hsatSet bridge extends satSet with reg/bind/same as state-local clauses), so determinism stays undefinable; time registers define determinism (Det-pm) but are blind to recurrence (star_invariance).
